Figure 2: Centralized vs. decentralized multi-agent systems. Centralized MAS relies on a main agent to assign subcontexts, spawn sub-agents, and integrate their results, so progress is shared mainly through the main agent and sub-agents remain unaware of one another’s work. In contrast, DELM decentralizes coordination through parallel agents, a shared context, and a task queue: agents asynchronously claim ready tasks, publish findings incrementally to a shared context, and build on or correct each other’s progress without a main agent in the loop.

checks.source_quote: Multi-agent systems (MAS) offer a natural way to scale large language model reasoning at test time: instead of solving a complex task in a single trajectory, they decompose it into subtasks, dispatch agents in parallel, and aggregate their progress (Anthropic, 2026, Feng et al., 2026, Hong et al., 2023, Kimi et al., 2026, OpenAI, 2025, Ruan et al., 2026, Zhang et al., 2025). This paradigm is increasingly important in agentic coding, both in repository-level software engineering (e.g., SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., 2024), DeepSWE (Huang and Jiang, 2026)), where agents can investigate different files, root causes, or fixes concurrently, and in interactive terminal tasks (e.g., Terminal-Bench (Merrill et al., 2026)), where agents can explore alternative solution paths while sharing what they learn about the environment. checks.assessment: 核对 bubble 定义：原文为“agent time that does not advance the solution”，包含“waiting on others”与“redoing work a peer has already done”两种来源，批注的“等待或重复工作时间”准确；“三类架构各自产生”也有原文“each of the three dominant families … creates them in its own way”支撑。术语借自 pipeline parallelism，批注未误称其为本文明确定义之外的东西。
checks.source_quote: Realizing this potential requires keeping every agent productive. Borrowing a term from pipeline parallelism (Huang et al., 2019), we call agent time that does not advance the solution a bubble: time an agent spends waiting on others, or redoing work a peer has already done. Bubbles waste compute and stretch wall-clock time, and each of the three dominant families of MAS creates them in its own way.

checks.assessment: 核对独立代理段：原文“never wait, but they share nothing”，气泡是“redundant work”，“adding agents adds compute, but much of it repeats exploration another agent has already done”。批注“无等待、缺共享、冗余”“新增算力主要被用于重复探索”是近似但正确的转述，未把作者未说的成本数字写入。
checks.source_quote: Independent agents run in parallel and select among their outputs, as in self-consistency (Wang et al., 2022), repeated sampling (Brown et al., 2024), and best-of-n sampling (Cobbe et al., 2021, Lightman et al., 2024). They never wait, but they share nothing while they run, so each agent must rediscover the same faults, fixes, and dead ends on its own. Their bubbles are redundant work: adding agents adds compute, but much of it repeats exploration another agent has already done.

checks.assessment: 核对对等通信段：straggler 来源表述（每轮由最慢代理决定、早完成者空闲）与原文一致；原文给出“n(n−1) messages per round”于全连接设置，批注概括为 $O(n^2)$ 属于同一量级的不同写法，不算错误；上下文膨胀亦有“each agent's context fills with peer responses it must read and reconcile”支撑。
checks.source_quote: Peer-communicating agents exchange responses over synchronous rounds, as in multi-agent debate (Chen et al., 2024, Du et al., 2023, Liang et al., 2023). Seeing peers’ answers lets agents correct one another, but each round is a barrier: its duration is set by the slowest agent, so agents that finish early sit idle. These barrier waits are the straggler problem familiar from bulk-synchronous parallel computing (Dean and Ghemawat, 2008, Valiant, 1990). Communication cost also grows with the number of agents: in the fully connected setting (Du et al., 2023), each agent ingests all n − 1 peer responses every round, for n(n − 1) messages per round, so each agent’s context fills with peer responses it must read and reconcile on its own.

A main agent decomposes the task, dispatches subtasks, waits for their outputs, and integrates the results (Figure 2, left). On Terminal-Bench 4.0’s retro-console-soc task (Figure 3), Claude Code’s main agent spends 73% of its time waiting on its subagents. Relaying can also lose information. checks.source_quote: We propose Decentralized Language Models (DELM), a MAS framework that squeezes out these bubbles by replacing the main agent with a shared problem state (Figure 2, right). DELM consists of parallel agents, a shared context, and a task queue, and each component targets one kind of bubble. Agents claim tasks from the queue asynchronously, so no agent waits at a round barrier or for a main agent to assign work. They publish compact findings to the shared context as soon as results are available, so peers build on intermediate progress instead of waiting for a relay. The queue and shared context also show what each agent is working on and which approaches have failed, so agents avoid redoing a peer’s work. Finally, corrections are appended as new entries rather than relayed through a main agent, so a fix reaches every agent without another round of delegation. Parallel agents asynchronously claim subtasks $\{ T _ { i } \}$ , read the shared context, and implement $\left\{ T _ { i } \right\}$ locally. checks.source_quote: Given a task D, DELM runs n agents concurrently, each with its own persistent session and workspace. Agents coordinate through two shared structures, a shared context C and a task queue T, and each agent produces its own complete solution.

checks.assessment: 五步操作的顺序与编号已逐条对照原文一致，异步的判据（一方发布时他人继续工作并可立即复用）也准确；原批注末句“最大化并行效率”是原文未给的目标函数式断言，已删除，改为不依赖全局同步这一可核对事实。
checks.source_quote: Figure 4 and Algorithm 1 summarize five operations: 1 initialize the task queue, 2 execute subtasks in parallel, 3 summarize and publish intermediate results, 4 update the task queue as work progresses, and 5 finalize each agent’s solution. These operations proceed asynchronously rather than in lockstep: while one agent publishes a result, others keep working and can reuse it as soon as it appears.

checks.assessment: 核对三类条目、FACT/FAIL 的 scope 与 evidence 字段、'keep entries brief' 与'state unfinished parts and known limitations'、附件与 conflict protection 合并，均与原文一致，未添加原文没有的条目类型。
checks.source_quote: The shared context C is an append-only log of reusable findings and contributions from all agents. Agents write to it through compact entries $G _ { i }$ of a declared type: a FACT records a finding supported by observations, a FAIL records an approach or hypothesis that was contradicted, and a completion summary records the result of a finished subtask. FACT and FAIL entries carry explicit scope and evidence fields; agents are instructed to keep entries brief and to state unfinished parts and known limitations, so that other agents can judge whether an entry applies to their own work. Any entry may attach files, which peers can inspect as diffs or merge into their own workspaces with conflict protection. Agents publish an entry as soon as a result is usable and then continue with their own work.

checks.assessment: 核对附件与摘要分开存储、发布时快照、expand 显示为相对原始任务文件的 diff、apply 拒绝覆盖无法解释的本地改动并留给接收方协调、读 C 只返回增量、按需分页类比指向附录 A.1，全部对得上；'条目正文'对应原文的 summary，措辞可接受。
checks.source_quote: Summaries with files by reference. An entry can attach files, which are stored separately from its summary and snapshotted at publication time. Agents inspect these files with expand, which shows them as diffs against the original task files, and copy selected files into their own workspace with apply. apply refuses to overwrite local changes it cannot account for, leaving reconciliation to the receiving agent. A read of C shows only what is new since that agent’s last read, namely new entries and changed work status, while older entries remain retrievable on demand. This design resembles demand paging in an operating system: agents follow progress through compact summaries and fetch detailed content from backing storage only when they need it (Appendix A.1).

checks.assessment: 核对检查项来源（原始任务而非子任务摘要）、复用同伴证据且不重复、聚焦未覆盖的需求与组件交互、条目不可变因而追加 FAIL、修正以新条目或修复子任务出现、提交前须解决相关未决失败，均与原文吻合，无额外主张。
checks.source_quote: Distributed verification and correction. Verification is left to the agents rather than to a central checker: each agent derives the checks for its own solution from the original task rather than from subtask summaries, reuses applicable evidence from its peers without repeating it, and directs additional checks at requirements and component interactions that existing evidence does not cover. Because entries are immutable, an agent that finds a defect in a shared result does not edit it. Instead, it appends a FAIL entry stating the conditions under which the defect occurs, and a correction follows as a new entry or a repair subtask. A FAIL stays open until it is addressed, and before submitting, each agent reads the shared context and resolves any published failure relevant to its own solution.

checks.assessment: 核对条目结构、四类需声明信息、建条目的三种许可情形、首个 agent 划范围与交接接管、此后任意 agent 可添加或认领、无特权规划者与无计划收尾。原批注把 'a concrete open question the solution depends on' 译为“有明确答案的开放问题”，与 concrete（具体）和 depends on 的含义不符，已改为“方案所依赖的具体开放问题”。
checks.source_quote: The task queue T divides the work among agents. Each item consists of a subject and a free-text detail, in which agents are instructed to state the intended output, its available inputs, the interface it shares with other work, and the earliest partial result it depends on. Agents are instructed to create items only for required implementation, repair of a demonstrated defect, or a concrete open question the solution depends on. At startup, the first agent reserves its own scope and publishes complementary items for its peers, or states the dependency that prevents a split; if it ends before this handoff, the next running agent takes over. After that, any agent can add items or claim open ones at any time. There is no privileged planner and no plan-closure step.

checks.assessment: 核对排他认领与先到先得、每 agent 至多一个未完成认领、open/claimed/done 与 owner、会话状态由框架追踪而非 agent 上报、依赖方活跃时先做独立工作仅有界等待、依赖方已结束时自建结果，均与原文一致。
checks.source_quote: Claims and status. The queue enforces exclusive claims: the first claim wins, and each agent holds at most one unfinished claim. Every item is marked open, claimed, or done, together with its owner, so each agent can see who is responsible for what and how much remains. Each read also shows every agent’s session state (starting, running, or ended), tracked by the framework rather than reported by the agents. Agents use this state to choose complementary work and to handle dependencies. If a dependency’s owner is starting or running, an agent continues with independent work and waits only when nothing else remains, using a bounded wait that returns as soon as a peer publishes or ends. If the owner of an item has ended without completing it, this does not block progress: an agent that needs the result builds it in its own workspace, reusing anything the owner already shared, instead of waiting.

checks.source_quote: When agents publish and read. Apart from session state, which the framework tracks automatically, all content in the shared context and task queue comes from the agents themselves: the framework never publishes on an agent’s behalf. An agent publishes when a result can unblock a peer, without needing to run new checks first, and avoids routine status updates and repeated evidence. checks.source_quote: These results show that multiple agents help even on largely sequential tasks. A single agent rarely completes every step correctly on its first attempt. It often inspects irrelevant files, pursues a wrong root cause, or submits a patch that fails the tests before it recovers. Each such detour costs time, and a single agent can only discover it by paying that cost itself. In DELM, agents explore different paths in parallel and record what they learn in the shared context. Once one agent has hit a dead end, the others can skip it, and once one has localized a fault, the others can build on that finding. This shortens the path to a correct fix, which explains why DELM is both faster and more accurate. A more detailed analysis is provided in Appendix D.

checks.source_quote: Removing peer-status awareness causes the largest slowdown under both models (0.87× and 0.82×), and with Claude Opus 5.5 it also causes the largest accuracy drop (−3.3 points). checks.source_quote: To understand how the coordination mechanisms in Table 1 squeeze out bubbles, we analyze all DELM runs on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE v1.1. checks.source_quote: Shared results help only if later improvements reach the agents that already used them. Because updates and corrections are appended as new entries that reference revised files, rather than overwriting old ones (§2.1), an agent can re-import a peer’s updated work at any time. Agents rely on this heavily. Across 720 agent trajectories on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE v1.1, agents imported shared files 5,237 times, and 80.3% of trajectories later imported a revised version of a file they had already imported. Agents thus track their peers’ work as it improves, and fixes reach every agent that depends on them without re-planning. In centralized systems, by contrast, correcting a result that has already been summarized and relayed requires another round of delegation.

checks.source_quote: This reuse is inexpensive. Because agents publish short summaries and attach files by reference (§2.1), the shared context averages under 15K tokens at task completion (Table 6). Each read also returns only what is new since the agent’s last read, so most of this content enters an agent’s session once. Accounting for all reads by all agents, including this cached reuse, reading the shared context accounts for 1.7–3.7% of total task cost with Claude Opus 5.5 and 7.7–17.7% with GPT-6-Astra.

CAMEL (Li et al., 2023) instantiates role-playing agents to study autonomous cooperation, while MetaGPT (Hong et al., 2023) and Chat-Dev (Qian et al., 2024) organize collaboration through software-engineering roles and standardized workflows. More recent systems make orchestration adaptive. AOrchestra (Ruan et al., 2026) creates task-specific sub-agents on demand, ToolOrchestra (Su et al., 2025) trains a lightweight orchestrator to coordinate models and tools, Squeeze Evolve (Maheswaran et al., 2026) routes the stages of evolutionary inference to models of different cost and capability, and RecursiveMAS (Yang et al., 2026b) replaces text-level communication with recursive latent-state transfer. checks.source_quote: Blackboard and shared-memory architectures. Blackboard architectures coordinate problem solvers through a shared workspace (Erman et al., 1980, Nii, 1986). Recent LLM variants use a blackboard on which agents post messages for general reasoning (Han and Zhang, 2025) or to which agents volunteer information in response to requests for data discovery (Salemi et al., 2025). However, these systems still rely on a control agent to select which agent acts or which request is posted, and they treat the board mainly as a message channel. DELM removes the controller from the loop entirely. Agents claim work asynchronously from a task queue, see what their peers are working on, and build on or correct earlier findings by appending to a stateful shared context (Table 1). We further target long-horizon agentic coding, where shared progress includes repository and environment state rather than only textual messages.

checks.assessment: 核对该段：SWE-agent 与 mini-SWE-agent 证明良好的 agent-computer interface 提升软件工程表现；Claude Code、Codex 属生产级 harness，可读仓库、改文件、执行命令并委派给原生子代理；Recursive Language Models 把 prompt 当作外部环境做代码中介循环。批注称 DELM 不替换单智能体循环而是叠加协调层，且原文明确 'we instantiate it on both Codex and Claude Code'，与批注一致。批注中“支持并行协作”是对 DELM 协调层用途的概括，原文此处未直接用 'parallel' 一词修饰 DELM，但结合上段任务队列并发认领的设定属合理概括，不构成事实错误。
checks.source_quote: Agentic coding harnesses. Language models become far more capable when coupled with executable environments that let them inspect state, invoke tools, and act on feedback. SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024) and its lightweight variant mini-SWE-agent show that a well-designed agent-computer interface substantially improves software-engineering performance. Production harnesses such as Claude Code (Anthropic, 2026) and Codex (OpenAI, 2025) let models read repositories, edit files, execute commands, and increasingly delegate work to native subagents. Recursive Language Models (Zhang et al., 2025) apply a similar code-mediated loop to long-context reasoning by treating the prompt as an external environment. DELM complements these harnesses: rather than replacing the single-agent loop, it adds a coordination layer on top of it, and we instantiate it on both Codex and Claude Code.

checks.source_quote: Conclusion. We introduced DELM, a decentralized multi-agent framework in which agents coordinate through a shared context and a task queue rather than through a main agent. By letting agents claim work asynchronously, publish findings as soon as they are usable, and see what every peer is doing, DELM squeezes out the bubbles that existing designs create: redundant work among independent agents, barrier waits among peer-communicating agents, and relay waits under centralized orchestration. Our ablation shows that these gains come from coordination rather than parallelism alone: removing any single mechanism brings two agents back to roughly single-agent speed. checks.source_quote: We therefore combine the two methods by retaining RLM as the underlying reasoner while adding two DELM components: a shared context and a decentralized task queue. In this hybrid setting, there is no main-agent/sub-agent hierarchy; all agents are equally ranked RLM instances that coordinate through shared state. An initial RLM call produces a compact work plan, after which subtasks are placed into the task queue and claimed by parallel RLM workers. Each worker’s output is admitted into the shared context, and the system then generates any additional subtasks from the current problem state, and computes the final answer from the shared context once no further subtasks are needed. This design preserves RLM’s strength in precise code-mediated execution while adding DELM’s decentralized coordination. As shown in Table 9, the combined method achieves the best accuracy and lowest cost on both benchmarks, indicating that RLM and DELM are complementary rather than competing approaches.

checks.source_quote: The shared context C is an append-only log of reusable findings and contributions from all agents. Agents write to it through compact entries $G _ { i }$ of a declared type: a FACT records a finding supported by observations, a FAIL records an approach or hypothesis that was contradicted, and a completion summary records the result of a finished subtask. FACT and FAIL entries carry explicit scope and evidence fields; agents are instructed to keep entries brief and to state unfinished parts and known limitations, so that other agents can judge whether an entry applies to their own work. Any entry may attach files, which peers can inspect as diffs or merge into their own workspaces with conflict protection. Agents publish an entry as soon as a result is usable and then continue with their own work.

checks.source_quote: Claims and status. The queue enforces exclusive claims: the first claim wins, and each agent holds at most one unfinished claim. Every item is marked open, claimed, or done, together with its owner, so each agent can see who is responsible for what and how much remains. Each read also shows every agent’s session state (starting, running, or ended), tracked by the framework rather than reported by the agents. Agents use this state to choose complementary work and to handle dependencies. If a dependency’s owner is starting or running, an agent continues with independent work and waits only when nothing else remains, using a bounded wait that returns as soon as a peer publishes or ends. If the owner of an item has ended without completing it, this does not block progress: an agent that needs the result builds it in its own workspace, reusing anything the owner already shared, instead of waiting.

With GPT-6-Astra, DELM (n=2) reaches 98.33% accuracy, 8.3 points above the strongest baseline, Codex with subagents (90.00%), and runs 1.25× faster than Codex. It also costs less per task than Codex with subagents (\$16.83 vs. \$24.97). With Claude Opus 5.5, the gains are larger: DELM (n=4) reaches 90.83%, 17.5 points above the strongest baseline, AOrchestra (73.33%), and runs 1.57× faster than Claude Code. DELM $\scriptstyle ( n = 2 )$ reaches 88.33% at roughly the same Cost/Task as Claude Code (\$12.15 vs. \$12.01).

checks.claim: SWE-bench Verified 上 DELM (n=4) 达 66.08%（+10.8 点，比 Claude Code 快 2.12×）
checks.assessment: 66.08%、+10.8 点与 2.12× 均可在该段逐字对上；2.12× 的参照是 Claude Code，已在卡片中写明，避免与相对 AOrchestra 的 1.47× 混淆。
checks.source_quote: SWE-bench Verified tests whether DELM still helps on a widely used software-engineering benchmark with a lightweight base model. We build DELM based on AOrchestra’s harness and compare it with Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent, and AOrchestra, all using Gemini 3 Flash. Table 5 shows that DELM outperforms all baselines in both accuracy and latency. With n = 4, DELM reaches 66.08% accuracy, 10.8 points higher than the strongest baseline, AOrchestra (55.26%). It is also 2.12× faster than Claude Code and 1.47× faster than AOrchestra. With n = 2, DELM still improves accuracy by 8.5 points over AOrchestra at the same Cost/Task (\$0.24), which halves the cost per submission. Going from n = 2 to n = 4 roughly doubles Cost/Task but leaves Cost/Submission unchanged at \$0.12, and it further improves both accuracy and latency.

checks.source_quote: 0.82–1.09×. Two parallel agents are thus no faster than one unless they coordinate effectively, so the speedup of DELM comes from coordination rather than from parallelism alone.

checks.claim: Terminal-Bench 上 n=4 准确率较 n=2 降 3–4 点
checks.assessment: 作者在 §3.1 就 Terminal-Bench 给出该降幅及其解释（每个 agent 仍提交完整方案、集成错误与缺陷扩散）。初稿未限定基准，与 DeepSWE 的 Table 3 数据冲突，已加限定。
checks.source_quote: Increasing to n=4 gives the largest speedups (2.05× and 2.49×): more work proceeds in parallel, and findings reach peers earlier. It also gives the lowest Cost/Submission, since each agent does a smaller share of the work and total cost grows more slowly than the number of submissions. Accuracy drops by 3–4 points relative to $n { = } 2 ,$ , because each agent still submits a complete solution while building less of it itself. More of each solution is assembled from peers’ components, which raises the risk of integration errors and lets a defect in one shared result affect several submissions. n=4 nonetheless remains above every baseline.

checks.source_quote: Because DELM targets long-horizon tasks where coordination matters, we evaluate on a subset of long-running tasks from Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE v1.1. We select tasks based on the wall-clock latency of Codex with GPT-6-Astra: for Terminal-Bench 4.0, we select 10 tasks with latency between 15 minutes and 1 hour; for DeepSWE v1.1, we select 10 tasks with latency of at least 10 minutes.
